items.value: Only two statements are correct — reducing maternal/neonatal mortality (2) and promoting institutional delivery (3)
items.reasoning: Janani Suraksha Yojana is a 100% centrally sponsored safe-motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission, not a scheme of the State Health Departments, so statement 1 is wrong. Statements 2 and 3 are the scheme's own stated objectives: reducing maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women. Statement 4 describes Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), which entitles sick infants up to one year of age to free treatment — that is a different scheme, not a JSY objective. Runner-up is C, which would follow if one credited statement 1 on the ground that States operationally implement JSY.

items.value: Only three are correct — delayed cord clamping, periodic deworming and addressing non-nutritional causes are all AMB interventions; the supplement is iron-folic acid, not calcium
items.reasoning: The Anaemia Mukt Bharat 6x6x6 strategy prescribes prophylactic IRON AND FOLIC ACID supplementation, not calcium, so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 2 is correct: ensuring delayed cord clamping at childbirth is part of the intensified year-round behaviour-change communication campaign. Statement 3 is correct: periodic deworming of children and adolescents is the second of the six interventions. Statement 4 reproduces the sixth intervention almost verbatim — addressing non-nutritional causes of anaemia in endemic pockets with special focus on malaria, haemoglobinopathies and fluorosis.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — carbon fibres are used in automobile and aircraft components, and they can be recycled
items.reasoning: Carbon-fibre reinforced composites are standard in aircraft primary structures and in high-performance automobile bodies and panels, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false: carbon fibre is recycled commercially by pyrolysis and solvolysis, which burn or dissolve away the polymer matrix and recover the fibre for reuse in shorter-fibre products. The recovered fibre is degraded in length and strength, but 'cannot be recycled' is an absolute claim the technology contradicts.

items.value: All three actions require an accelerometer
items.reasoning: An accelerometer measures proper acceleration, and all three cases are acceleration events. A collision produces a very large deceleration spike, which is what the airbag crash sensor detects to fire the inflator. A laptop in free fall registers near-zero proper acceleration in every axis, which is the signature the sudden-motion sensor uses to park the hard-disk head. A stationary phone's accelerometer reads the 1g gravity vector, and the direction of that vector relative to the device tells the software whether the screen is portrait or landscape.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — biofilters nitrify ammonia to nitrate; they do not remove solid feed waste or add phosphorus
items.reasoning: In a Recirculating Aquaculture System, solids such as uneaten feed and faeces are removed upstream by MECHANICAL filtration (settling basins, drum or screen filters); the biofilter handles dissolved waste, so statement 1 misattributes the job and is wrong. Statement 2 is the biofilter's actual function: nitrifying bacteria oxidise toxic ammonia to nitrite and then to far less toxic nitrate. Statement 3 is wrong on two counts — biofilters do not generate phosphorus, and phosphorus accumulation in RAS water is a waste-management problem, not a nutrient supplied to fish. Runner-up is B, which would follow only if 'waste treatment' in statement 1 were read loosely enough to cover solids removal.

items.value: Only the Pulsars pair is correctly matched; the descriptions of Cepheids and Nebulae are swapped
items.reasoning: Cepheids are pulsating variable STARS that brighten and dim on a regular period — the description printed against Nebulae — so pair 1 is wrong. Nebulae are the giant clouds of dust and gas — the description printed against Cepheids — so pair 2 is wrong; the two descriptions have simply been interchanged. Pair 3 is correct: a pulsar is a rapidly rotating, highly magnetised neutron star formed when a massive star exhausts its fuel and its core collapses.

items.value: Japan, which operates the Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS / Michibiki)
items.reasoning: Japan runs QZSS, a regional satellite navigation and augmentation constellation in quasi-zenith orbits designed to give high-elevation coverage over Japan and the Asia-Oceania region. Australia and Canada operate no navigation constellation of their own and rely on GPS (Australia's SBAS project is a ground-based augmentation of other systems, not a satellite navigation system it owns). Israel has substantial space and satellite capability but no navigation constellation.

items.value: Neither statement is correct — both reverse the descriptions of ballistic and cruise missiles
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is inverted: it is the CRUISE missile that is air-breathing jet-propelled through most of its flight, often at subsonic speed, while the BALLISTIC missile is rocket-powered only in its initial boost phase and thereafter follows an unpowered ballistic trajectory. Statement 2 is also inverted: Agni-V is a solid-fuelled long-range ballistic missile, while BrahMos is the supersonic cruise missile. Since each statement attaches each description to the wrong missile type, neither is correct.

items.value: All three are correct — gold mining and coal-fired power are mercury sources, and no exposure level is regarded as safe
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: artisanal and small-scale gold mining, which uses mercury amalgamation to extract gold from ore, is the single largest source of anthropogenic mercury release worldwide. Statement 2 is correct: coal contains trace mercury that is volatilised on combustion, making coal-fired power stations a leading source of atmospheric mercury emissions. Statement 3 reflects the standard public-health position that no threshold of mercury exposure has been established below which harm does not occur, particularly for methylmercury and the developing nervous system. Runner-up is B, which would follow if statement 3's absolute wording were judged an overstatement.

items.value: All three are correct — green hydrogen can be burnt directly, blended with natural gas, and used in fuel cells
items.reasoning: Hydrogen is a combustible fuel and hydrogen internal-combustion engines are a demonstrated technology, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: hydrogen is blended into natural gas pipelines at low percentages and burnt for heat or power, and such blending trials are a core part of hydrogen roadmaps. Statement 3 is correct: the hydrogen fuel cell electrochemically combines hydrogen with oxygen to generate electricity for fuel-cell electric vehicles. Green hydrogen differs from other hydrogen only in how it is produced (electrolysis using renewable electricity), so every end use available to hydrogen is available to it.

items.value: Only two — Hungary and Romania share a land border with Ukraine
items.reasoning: Ukraine's land neighbours are Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania and Moldova. From the list given, only Hungary and Romania are among them. Bulgaria is separated from Ukraine by Romania; the Czech Republic is separated by Slovakia; and Latvia and Lithuania are separated by Belarus, which lies between the Baltic states and Ukraine.

items.value: Infrared waves are largely absorbed by water vapour concentrated in the lower atmosphere
items.reasoning: Water vapour is the atmosphere's most important infrared absorber and is overwhelmingly concentrated in the lower troposphere, which is why the lower atmosphere is heated largely from below rather than directly by incoming solar radiation — so C is correct. A overstates the equator-to-pole insolation ratio, which is of the order of four times, not ten. B is wrong because infrared makes up roughly half of insolation, not two-thirds. D is wrong by definition: infrared lies beyond the red end of the visible spectrum and is not part of it.

items.value: Statement-I is incorrect (rainforest soils are nutrient-poor) but Statement-II is correct
items.reasoning: Tropical rainforest soils are characteristically nutrient-POOR: heavy rainfall leaches soluble bases from the profile, and almost all the nutrient stock of the ecosystem is locked up in the living biomass rather than the soil, so Statement-I is false. Statement-II is true — persistently high temperature and moisture make decomposer activity extremely rapid, so litter breaks down quickly. Note that Statement-II is in fact part of the reason Statement-I is false: fast decomposition combined with immediate root uptake and leaching leaves little organic matter to accumulate in the soil.

items.value: Statement-I is incorrect (the land-sea temperature contrast is greater in winter) but Statement-II is correct
items.reasoning: Water's high specific heat and its ability to mix heat through depth make the ocean thermally sluggish, so Statement-II is true. But the resulting contrast is at its largest in WINTER, not summer: continental interiors in the northern hemisphere cool to extreme lows under clear skies, snow cover and inversions while the ocean at the same latitude stays near its annual mean, which is why January isotherms bend sharply where they cross coastlines whereas July isotherms run far closer to the parallels. Statement-I therefore reverses the seasonal comparison. Runner-up is A, which would follow if the summer land-sea heating contrast (the one usually invoked to explain the monsoon) were taken as the larger.

items.value: Both are correct — P waves arrive first, and P waves are longitudinal while S waves are transverse
items.reasoning: P (primary) waves travel faster than S (secondary) waves through the same medium, so a seismograph records them earlier — that is exactly how the P-S arrival interval is used to estimate distance to the epicentre. Statement 2 gives the standard description of the two wave types: P waves are longitudinal, with particles oscillating back and forth along the direction of propagation, while S waves are transverse, with particles oscillating at right angles to it. 'Up and down' is the conventional textbook depiction of that transverse motion.

items.value: None of the statements is correct — all three 'none of them' claims are false
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false: coastal coal-fired stations use seawater for once-through condenser cooling, and several Indian coastal plants do so. Statement 2 is false: a well-documented share of India's coal fleet sits in districts classed as water-stressed, which is precisely why freshwater withdrawal norms were tightened for thermal plants. Statement 3 is false: a large part of India's installed coal capacity is privately owned by companies such as Tata Power, Adani Power and JSW Energy, alongside NTPC and the State generating companies. Each statement is an absolute 'none of them' claim, and a single counter-example defeats each.

items.value: Controlling viral diseases spread by mosquitoes
items.reasoning: The Wolbachia method introduces the naturally occurring bacterium Wolbachia into Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacterium competes with viruses inside the insect and sharply reduces the mosquito's ability to transmit dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever; because Wolbachia is passed from female mosquitoes to their offspring, it spreads through the wild population once released. The other options concern crop residues, bioplastics and biochar and have nothing to do with the technique.

items.value: All three are discussed as carbon capture and sequestration approaches
items.reasoning: Spreading finely ground basalt on farmland is enhanced rock weathering: the silicate minerals react with dissolved carbon dioxide and lock it away as bicarbonate, and it is actively trialled as a carbon-removal method. Adding lime to raise ocean alkalinity is ocean alkalinity enhancement, which increases the sea's capacity to absorb and retain carbon dioxide. Capturing industrial carbon dioxide and injecting it underground, including dissolved in water so that it mineralises in the host rock, is conventional geological sequestration. All three appear routinely in the carbon-capture-and-sequestration literature.

items.value: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
items.reasoning: Metagenomics means sequencing genetic material recovered directly from an environmental sample rather than from a cultured or captured organism, so 'aerial metagenomics' means filtering airborne environmental DNA and reading in one pass the genetic traces of every organism that shed material into that air. Option B describes ornithological genomics, C describes remote blood sampling, and D describes drone-based physical specimen collection — none of these is sequencing an environmental sample of the air itself.

items.value: Studying the evolutionary relationships among various species of fauna
items.reasoning: Microsatellites are short tandemly repeated DNA motifs whose repeat number is highly variable between individuals and populations, which makes them standard markers for identity, parentage, population structure and the genetic distances used to reconstruct relationships among related taxa. The other options describe unrelated techniques: stem-cell differentiation is driven by growth factors and culture conditions, clonal propagation is a tissue-culture method, and drug efficacy is assessed by clinical trials — none of them is a DNA marker application.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — all bank loans to MSMEs qualify as priority sector; the medium-enterprise investment band is not 15-25 crore
items.reasoning: Statement 1 matches no version of the definition. Under the MSMED Act, 2006 as originally enacted, a medium manufacturing enterprise was one with investment in plant and machinery above 5 crore and up to 10 crore rupees; under the revised composite criteria a medium enterprise is one with investment up to 50 crore and turnover up to 250 crore. The band of 15 to 25 crore is neither. Statement 2 is correct: the Reserve Bank's priority sector lending norms provide that all bank loans to micro, small and medium enterprises qualify for classification under the priority sector.

items.value: Both are correct — a CBDC can settle payments outside the dollar and SWIFT, and can carry programmed conditions such as a spending deadline
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: a central bank digital currency can be transferred directly on the issuing central bank's own ledger or through bilateral and multilateral CBDC platforms, bypassing correspondent banking, dollar clearing and the SWIFT messaging network — which is a large part of why central banks are interested in it. Statement 2 is correct: programmability is a defining feature under discussion, allowing a unit to carry embedded conditions such as an expiry date, a permitted category of merchant, or a restricted purpose, which is how expiring digital-currency stimulus distributions have been piloted.

items.value: A numeric value measuring how a stock's fluctuations respond to changes in the overall market
items.reasoning: Beta measures a security's systematic risk — the sensitivity of its returns to movements of the market as a whole. A beta of 1 means the stock tends to move with the market, above 1 that it amplifies market moves, and below 1 that it is less volatile than the market. Option A describes arbitrage, option B describes portfolio construction or asset allocation generally, and option C describes basis risk; none of them is what the coefficient beta denotes.

items.value: Only two are correct — joint responsibility for a member's loan (2) and support from RRBs and commercial banks (3); the programme was not initiated by SBI
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD, which began the pilot linking self-help groups to banks in 1992, building on earlier work by voluntary agencies — not by the State Bank of India. Statement 2 is correct and is the core of the model: lending is to the group and the members are jointly responsible, which is what substitutes for collateral. Statement 3 is correct: commercial banks, regional rural banks and cooperative banks are all participating lenders under the linkage programme.

items.value: Both statements are correct, but the States' primary responsibility for health services does not explain the curative focus
items.reasoning: Statement-I is correct and is the standard critique underlying the shift to Health and Wellness Centres: public health spending has been weighted towards curative, facility-based care, with preventive, promotive and especially rehabilitative services thinly provided. Statement-II is correct because public health and hospitals are a State subject and the States organise and run health services. But the two are independent facts — a curative bias is a matter of how resources and programmes are designed and is found irrespective of which tier delivers care, so decentralisation is not its cause. Runner-up is A if one accepted that fragmented State-level delivery is what produces the curative bias.
